circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island, has served as the venue for the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix season finale since 2009. It was the second Formula One circuit established in the Middle East, following Bahrain and preceding tracks in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb winds around the nearby lake and serves as the venue for the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year, alongside various supporting motorsport categories. The track holds an FIA Grade 1 classification, qualifying it as a premier international racing facility.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, the Red Bull Ring is a 4. 326 km circuit that has hosted the Austrian Grand Prix across two distinct periods, first from 1970 to 1987 as the Österreichring and later from 1997 to 2003 following its reconstruction and renaming as the A1-Ring.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: Located on a street circuit in Baku, Azerbaijan, the Baku City Circuit stretches 6. 003 km, ranking as the fourth-longest track in Formula One. The venue first hosted a Grand Prix in 2016 as the European Grand Prix, before becoming the home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and hosted the first Formula One race ever held in the Middle East that same year. The FIA Grade 1-licensed venue accommodates various motorsport categories including the annual Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix, GP2 racing, and 24-hour endurance competitions, with multiple circuit configurations available for different racing formats.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, located near Barcelona in northeastern Spain, spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straights and varied corner configurations that test multiple aspects of driver skill. Holding an FIA Grade 1 license with spectator capacity exceeding 140,000, the venue represents a comprehensive challenge for Formula One competition.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Situated in Wallonia near the town of Spa, this 7. 004 km Belgian circuit has been a fixture of Formula One racing since the sport's inaugural 1950 season. The venue has hosted the Belgian Grand Prix continuously since 1985, with only two absences in 2003 and 2006, making it one of the championship's most enduring grand prix locations.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: The Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km temporary motor racing track located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, which annually hosts the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the venue has accommodated various international motorsporting competitions, including World Sportscar Championship events and multiple North American racing series.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading district, this Chinese motorsport facility gained prominence as the home of the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually between 2004 and 2019 before resuming in 2024. In addition to hosting the Formula One race, the venue began staging the Shanghai ePrix championship from 2024 onwards.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near villages in Northamptonshire, Silverstone has been England's premier racing venue since hosting the inaugural British Grand Prix in 1948, followed by the opening round of the inaugural Formula One World Championship in 1950. After alternating with two other British circuits for over three decades, the British Grand Prix became a permanent fixture at Silverstone from 1987 onwards.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Mogyoród, is a 4. 381 km permanent circuit that hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix held within the Eastern Bloc in 1986. Constructed in just eight months, faster than any other F1 venue, the track was built outside the city after the Hungarian government rejected plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Monza Circuit is a 5. 793 km track constructed in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built motor racing facility. The venue, nicknamed "the Temple of Speed" for its emphasis on fast, flowing sections, has hosted the Italian Grand Prix annually since 1949, missing only the 1980 season due to renovations, making it one of Formula One's most enduring grand prix locations since the championship's inception.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit, a 5. 807 km track in Mie Prefecture, Japan, serves as a major venue for Formula One and Super Formula racing. Operated by Honda Mobilityland, the facility can accommodate 155,000 spectators and is renowned as one of the premier racing destinations in international motorsport.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that weaves through Paradise, Nevada, incorporating major thoroughfares and iconic casino resorts along Las Vegas Boulevard. The track passes by recognizable venues including the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas as it navigates the urban landscape.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Mexico City's Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, a 4. 304 km circuit, commemorates two tragic racing brothers through its name, honoring Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez who died in racing accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The track has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix since 2015 on its current layout, though it previously held the event on different configurations until 1992, with the race currently branded as the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit built around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners and qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One, it became home to the Miami Grand Prix when the event joined the calendar in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street circuit that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts of Monaco, following routes around the harbour area. The venue is widely known by the name "Monte Carlo," reflecting the prominence of this neighbourhood within the track's layout.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes west of Amsterdam, the Zandvoort circuit stretches 4. 259 km and hosted the Dutch Grand Prix after rejoining the Formula One calendar in 2021 following a lengthy absence. The venue's partnership with the sport concluded in 2026.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit sits just north of Doha in Qatar and spans 5. 419 kilometres with a 1. 068-kilometre main straight, holding an FIA Grade 1 license.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos, a 4. 309 km Brazilian circuit in São Paulo, opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace following his 1977 death in a plane crash. The anticlockwise track hosts major racing events and features a karting facility dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: This Saudi Arabian street circuit, positioned along Jeddah's waterfront promenade overlooking the Red Sea, has served as the venue for the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its inaugural running in 2021. The venue also hosts international electric racing events, beginning with Formula E races in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit is an urban racing venue that winds through Singapore's Marina Bay area, incorporating the Downtown Core and Kallang districts within its layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in northeastern Spain, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya stretches 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations that test multiple driving skills. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located near Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 5. 514-kilometer Grade 1 track that serves as the permanent home of the United States Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the facility hosts major international racing events including MotoGP's Americas round, the Lone Star Le Mans endurance race, and NASCAR competitions, while previously welcoming various other motorsport series.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon, a Thai and British racing driver, currently races for Williams under the Thai flag in Formula One.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, bringing two world championship titles won with Renault in 2005 and 2006 along with 32 career Grand Prix victories spanning 23 seasons. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans victories with Toyota, the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, and the 2019 Daytona 24 Hours, making him the sole competitor to have won both F1 and World Endurance world titles.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli joined Mercedes' Formula One lineup in 2025 and has already secured eight Grand Prix victories during his early career in the sport.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British motorsport competitor who currently races for Haas in Formula One's elite championship series.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One as a driver for Audi.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: The Finnish driver competes for Cadillac in Formula One after a lengthy career that included two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during consecutive seasons while with Mercedes. Across 13 campaigns in the sport, he has secured 10 Grand Prix victories.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently competing in Formula One with Alpine, representing his country in the sport's top racing series.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, holds a reserve role at Haas while actively competing in European Le Mans Series prototypes for Nielsen Racing. He has appeared in seven Formula One races between 2024 and 2025.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. He previously achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a French-Algerian driver who races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, representing France.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British driver competing for Ferrari who has achieved seven world championships, matching Michael Schumacher's record. He holds multiple Formula One records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: Nicolas Hülkenberg, a German driver, currently races in Formula One for Audi. The accomplished motorsport competitor achieved victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport competitor who currently drives for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc is a Monégasque driver currently racing for Ferrari in Formula One. He finished as championship runner-up in 2022 and has secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine seasons in the sport.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Danish driver Kevin Magnussen raced in Formula One across two separate periods spanning 2014-2020 and 2022-2024, before transitioning to other series. He currently competes in the World Endurance Championship with BMW through WRT and pursues part-time NASCAR commitments with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver competing for McLaren in Formula One, claimed the 2025 World Drivers' Championship title. The accomplished racer has secured 13 Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon, a French racing driver, currently competes in Formula One for the Haas team.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from 15 seasons in the sport. He finished second in the 2023 drivers' championship while at Red Bull and has secured six race victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver, races for McLaren in Formula One and has achieved nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four-season tenure in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: The Australian driver competed in Formula One between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories throughout his 14-year career in the sport. Known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," Ricciardo has since retired from the championship.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell has secured eight Grand Prix victories throughout his Formula One career, which he continues with Mercedes.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to sports car racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously driven LMP2 vehicles for Era Motorsport in IMSA competition.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One competitor who drives for Aston Martin in the sport's top tier.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese driver currently holding reserve duties with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in Formula One. He competed as a full-time driver from 2021 through 2025 before transitioning to a reserve role in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen has secured four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024 while racing for Red Bull Racing. Over his 12-season tenure in Formula One, he has accumulated 72 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu represents China as the sole Chinese driver to have raced in Formula One, having competed in the sport from 2022 through 2024. He currently holds a reserve driver position with the Cadillac Formula One team.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team competed as Renault's official works entry before rebranding as Alpine in 2021 to showcase the French manufacturer's sports car division. Operating under various sponsorship arrangements, Alpine maintained Renault's works status until the automotive company's Formula One withdrawal concluded at the end of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has a storied presence in Formula One through multiple incarnations, with the modern entity operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco branding in the championship.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari represents the motorsport arm of the Italian luxury carmaker Ferrari and maintains the distinction of being Formula One's longest-established and most accomplished team, having participated in every championship season since the sport's inception in 1950. The squad is colloquially referred to by the emblematic name associated with their brand identity.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: TGR Haas F1 Team is an American-licensed outfit founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas, entering Formula One competition in 2016. Ayao Komatsu currently leads the team as principal, taking over the role from Guenther Steiner, who departed in early 2024 after overseeing the squad since its establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss engineering firm established in 1970, this constructor initially excelled in endurance racing before entering Formula One in 1993. The team competed in the sport for over three decades, becoming one of the oldest active constructors by race entries, before being acquired by Audi in 2024 and transitioning to form the foundation of Audi's F1 program.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that operates under the McLaren Group's ownership structure, ultimately controlled by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a continuous presence in Formula One since 1954 through team ownership and engine supply. The current Mercedes-AMG Petronas operation, based in Brackley with a German racing licence, became jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff from 2022 onwards. The marque's racing heritage is synonymous with the "Silver Arrows" nickname.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that commenced competition in 2024, based in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes. As one of two Red Bull GmbH-owned constructors alongside Red Bull Racing, it operates as a sister team within the Austrian conglomerate's motorsport portfolio.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the sport in 2024 as the second team under Red Bull GmbH's ownership, alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with an additional facility near its sister team's base in Milton Keynes, the squad operates as a distinct entity within the Red Bull organization's two-team structure.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, an Austrian-licensed team headquartered in England, has been a prominent Formula One outfit since its 2005 establishment under the ownership of Red Bull GmbH. Led by Christian Horner throughout its two-decade history until his 2025 departure, the team was succeeded in leadership by Laurent Mekies, while the parent company also operates a second F1 team, Racing Bulls.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering stands as a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's earlier failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in 2026 under the Atlassian Williams F1 Team banner and operates from a substantial 60-acre facility.
